algorithm: Human Action Transformer (HAT), an ACT-style action-chunking transformer co-trained jointly on unified human (PH2D) and teleoperated-robot demonstrations in a shared 54-D wrist-pose + fingertip state-action space
headline_metric: real-robot task success rate, in-distribution (I.D.) vs. out-of-distribution (O.O.D.)
headline_value: overall I.D.: ACT 42/60 vs. HAT (with data norm) 49/60; overall O.O.D.: ACT 59/170 vs. HAT (with data norm) 101/170, ~100% relative improvement OOD (Table 2)
human_data: own PH2D egocentric demonstrations collected via consumer VR devices (Apple Vision Pro / Meta Quest 3, optionally a ZED stereo camera), language-instructed, not internet video
operator_interface: consumer VR headsets (Apple Vision Pro built-in camera with ARKit hand/head tracking, or Meta Quest 3/Vision Pro with a 3D-printed ZED Mini stereo mount via an OpenTelevision web app), <$700; robot-side demonstrations collected via standard humanoid teleoperation
retargeting_objective: no offline kinematic retargeting network; human and robot share an identical 54-D state-action space via a bijective fingertip-to-fingertip correspondence (both are 5-fingered hands), bridged only by action-speed interpolation (human trajectories slowed ~4x) and instructing operators to minimize torso movement
